The San Luis Obispo Superior Court is the main trial court in the county of San Luis Obispo, California. The court has jurisdiction over criminal and civil cases, as well as family law, probate, and juvenile cases. This article will provide a comprehensive guide to the San Luis Obispo Superior Court, including its history, structure, services, and procedures.

History of the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court was established in 1850, shortly after California became a state. The court originally held sessions in the county courthouse, which was built in 1852. Over the years, the court has undergone many changes, including the construction of a new courthouse in 1940 and the addition of a new courthouse in 2010. Today, the San Luis Obispo Superior Court is a modern and efficient court system that serves the needs of the community.

Structure of the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court is divided into several divisions, each with its own presiding judge. The divisions include the Criminal Division, the Civil Division, the Family Law Division, the Probate Division, and the Juvenile Division. Each division is responsible for hearing cases within its jurisdiction and ensuring that justice is served. The court also has a number of judges, commissioners, and staff members who work together to keep the court running smoothly.

Services Provided by the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court provides a wide range of services to the community, including access to legal information and resources, assistance with court filings, and access to court records. The court also provides services for those who are representing themselves in court, including self-help centers and workshops. In addition, the court offers alternative dispute resolution services, such as mediation and arbitration, to help parties resolve their disputes outside of court.

Criminal Cases in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court handles a wide range of criminal cases, including misdemeanors, felonies, and traffic violations. The court is responsible for ensuring that justice is served in these cases, and that defendants are given a fair trial. The court also provides services to victims of crime, including victim/witness assistance programs.

Civil Cases in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court also handles civil cases, including cases involving contract disputes, personal injury, and property damage. The court is responsible for ensuring that all parties are given a fair hearing and that justice is served. The court also provides services to help parties resolve their disputes outside of court, such as mediation and arbitration.

Family Law Cases in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court handles a wide range of family law cases, including divorce, child custody, and domestic violence. The court is responsible for ensuring that the best interests of the children and families involved are protected and that a fair resolution is reached. The court provides a range of services to assist parties in these cases, including mediation, counseling, and parenting classes.

Probate Cases in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court also handles probate cases, which involve the distribution of assets and the settlement of debts after a person has passed away. The court is responsible for ensuring that the wishes of the deceased are carried out and that any disputes among family members or other parties are resolved fairly. The court also provides services to assist parties in these cases, including access to legal information and assistance with court filings.

Juvenile Cases in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court handles juvenile cases, which involve minors who have been accused of committing crimes or who are involved in other legal proceedings. The court is responsible for ensuring that the best interests of the minors are protected and that they are given the help and support they need to get back on track. The court provides a range of services to assist minors and their families in these cases, including counseling, education, and community service programs.

Procedures in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court has established procedures for filing cases, appearing in court, and resolving disputes. Parties are encouraged to consult with an attorney or access self-help services to ensure that they understand these procedures and can navigate the court system effectively. The court also provides information and resources on its website and through other channels to help parties prepare for their court appearance.

Resources for the San Luis Obispo Superior Court

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court provides a wide range of resources to help parties navigate the court system and access the services they need. These resources include self-help centers, legal aid organizations, and online tools and forms. The court also provides access to court records and other public information through its website and other channels.

San Luis Obispo Superior Court Case Search

If you are looking for information about a specific case in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court, you can easily search for it online. The court provides an online case search tool that allows you to search for cases by name, case number, or filing date. This tool is available 24/7 and is free to use. Simply go to the court's website and click on the "Case Search" tab to get started.

San Luis Obispo Court Records Criminal

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court maintains records of all criminal cases that are heard in the county. These records are available to the public and can be accessed through the court's online case search tool. You can search for criminal records by name, case number, or filing date. If you need a certified copy of a criminal record, you can request it from the court's Records Department.

San Luis Obispo Court Docket

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court maintains a docket of all cases that are scheduled to be heard in the court. The docket is updated daily and can be accessed online through the court's website. You can search for cases by date, time, and case type. The docket also provides information about the judge assigned to each case.

San Luis Obispo Court Filing

If you need to file a document with the San Luis Obispo Superior Court, you can do so either in person or online. The court's e-filing system allows you to file documents electronically from anywhere with an internet connection. You can also file documents in person at the court's filing window. The court accepts filings for all types of cases, including civil, criminal, family, and probate.

San Luis Obispo Superior Court – Civil Case Search

If you are looking for information about a civil case in the San Luis Obispo Superior Court, you can search for it online using the court's case search tool. The tool allows you to search for cases by name, case number, or filing date. You can also search for cases by case type, such as small claims or family law. The court's civil case search tool is available 24/7 and is free to use.

San Luis Obispo Superior Court Attorney Portal

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court provides an attorney portal for attorneys who practice in the county. The portal allows attorneys to access their cases online, file documents electronically, and view the court's docket. Attorneys can also sign up for electronic notifications and receive updates about their cases via email or text message.

San Luis Obispo Superior Court Phone Number

If you need to contact the San Luis Obispo Superior Court, you can do so by phone. The court's main phone number is (805) 781-5670. You can also find phone numbers for specific court departments, such as the Records Department and the Traffic Division, on the court's website.

San Luis Obispo Court Calendar

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court maintains a calendar of all court proceedings that are scheduled to take place in the county. The calendar is updated daily and can be accessed online through the court's website. You can search for court dates by date, time, and case type. The calendar also provides information about the location of each court proceeding.

Overview of the Court System

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court is part of the California state court system. This court has jurisdiction over all civil, criminal, traffic, family law, probate, and juvenile cases arising in San Luis Obispo County. The court system serves to uphold local laws, resolve legal disputes, and deliver justice.

There are over 30 judicial officers and 150 support staff across multiple court locations in the county. The court system strives to provide equal access to justice through fair, timely, and efficient case processing and resolution.

Locations and Services

In addition to the Civil & Family Law Branch, the San Luis Obispo Superior Court has several other locations:

  • Criminal Branch – Handles criminal cases and traffic matters
  • Grover Beach Branch – Focuses on traffic cases
  • Juvenile Services Center – Addresses juvenile delinquency matters
  • Paso Robles Branch – Covers civil and family law cases
  • Veteran's Memorial Branch – Deals with traffic violations (temporarily closed)

Each branch focuses on specific legal needs of local residents based on case type and jurisdiction. But collectively they enable the Superior Court to deliver justice across a wide spectrum of legal issues.

Civil & Family Law Branch

The Civil & Family Law Branch is located at:

1050 Monterey Street, Room 220
San Luis Obispo, CA 93408

This branch handles all civil and family law matters in the region, including:

  • Civil lawsuits and disputes
  • Family law cases (divorce, child custody, etc.)
  • Probate of estates

With experienced staff and judicial officers, the Civil & Family Law Branch provides professional and responsive services for important legal proceedings.

Criminal Branch

The Criminal Branch is housed in the same building as the Civil Branch, at 1050 Monterey Street, Room 220 in San Luis Obispo.

This branch oversees all criminal cases and traffic matters arising within its jurisdictional boundaries. The Criminal Branch handles proceedings including:

  • Criminal arraignments and trials
  • Traffic ticket hearings and trials
  • Misdemeanor and felony matters
  • Juvenile delinquency cases

Grover Beach Branch

The Grover Beach Branch is located at:

214 South 16th Street
Grover Beach, CA 93433

This branch exclusively handles traffic citation matters arising in Grover Beach. Services include traffic arraignments and trials. The streamlined focus on traffic violations allows efficient case resolution.

Juvenile Services Center

The Juvenile Services Center is located at 1050 Monterey Street in San Luis Obispo.

This center manages all juvenile justice matters, including delinquency cases. Juvenile court proceedings aim to rehabilitate youth offenders and promote positive development.

Paso Robles Branch

901 Park Street
Paso Robles, CA 93446

The Paso Robles Branch handles civil and family law matters arising in and around Paso Robles. This provides greater access to justice for northern San Luis Obispo residents.

Veteran’s Memorial Branch

801 Grand Ave.
San Luis Obispo, CA 93408

The Veteran's Branch focuses exclusively on traffic cases in San Luis Obispo. It is temporarily closed but typically provides efficient case management for local traffic violations.

Key Services Provided

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court system handles a wide range of legal matters to meet the needs of the community. Some of the key services include:

Civil Cases

The Civil Divisions and Branches handle all types of civil disputes, including:

  • Contract disputes
  • Personal injury and property damage
  • Malpractice and professional liability
  • Business and commercial litigation
  • Debt collection
  • Landlord/tenant issues

Civil cases aim to determine liability and award damages where appropriate.

Criminal Cases

The Criminal Branches process criminal allegations under state law, including:

  • Violent crimes (assault, battery, murder)
  • Property crimes (theft, fraud, vandalism)
  • Drug offenses
  • DUI/DWI
  • Weapons violations
  • Sex crimes

Criminal cases hold offenders accountable through prosecution and sentencing.

Traffic Cases

Traffic branches adjudicate all traffic citation matters, including:

  • Speeding tickets
  • Stop sign/red light violations
  • DUI
  • Driving with suspended license
  • At-fault accidents

Resolving traffic violations maintains road safety and accountability.

Family Law

Family Law Branches handle legal family matters like:

  • Divorce and separation
  • Child custody and visitation
  • Alimony and child support
  • Paternity judgments
  • Adoptions

Family law ensures fair legal resolutions to family and domestic issues.

Probate

Probate divisions assist with estates of deceased persons, including:

  • Will validation
  • Executor appointments
  • Estate administration
  • Asset distribution
  • Inheritance disputes

Probate provides orderly, lawful estate settlement.

Juvenile Justice

The Juvenile Services Center handles all juvenile delinquency matters, including:

  • Truancy
  • Underage drinking
  • Curfew violations
  • Property damage
  • Theft
  • Assault

The juvenile justice system aims to rehabilitate youth within the law.

Contacting the Court

To access services or get information, the public can contact the San Luis Obispo Superior Court branches by phone or in person during business hours:

Phone Hours

All branches share the phone number: (805) 706-3600

Phone lines are open Monday – Friday, from 8:30 am – 4:00 pm.

Individual branches have specified phone menu options to reach appropriate staff.

Counter Hours

Court branches are open for in-person assistance Monday – Friday, 8:30 am – 12:00 pm. Visitors can speak directly with clerks and access public records.

Getting Directions

Each branch lists its full street address to enable the public to get directions and locate the appropriate court facility. Addresses are also available on the court website and Google Maps.

Conclusion

The San Luis Obispo Superior Court plays a vital role in ensuring that justice is served in the community. With its dedicated judges, staff, and resources, the court provides a range of services to help parties navigate the court system and resolve their disputes fairly. Whether you are involved in a criminal, civil, family law, probate, or juvenile case, the San Luis Obispo Superior Court is here to help.
